summary: The Petitioner, Power Grid Corporation of India Limited, has filed the instant Petition for - _“1) Condone the delay in the commissioning of assets covered under this petition._ _3) Admit the capital cost as claimed in the Petition and approve the Additional Capitalization incurred / projected to be incurred._ - _4) Allow the petitioner to recover the shortfall or refund the excess Annual Fixed Charges, on account of Return on Equity due to change in applicable Minimum Alternate/Corporate Income Tax rate as per the Income Tax Act, 1961 (as amended from time to time) of the respective financial year directly without making any application before the Commission as provided in Tariff Regulation 2019 as per para 8 above for respective block._ _and pass such other relief as the Commission deems fit and appropriate under the circumstances of the case and in the interest of justice.”_ 6. This order is issued considering the submissions made by the Petitioner in the Petition vide affidavits dated 20.6.2022, 10.10.2023, 5.1.2024 and 15.3.2024, replies filed by MPPMCL and MSEDCL vide affidavits dated 19.1.2024 and 29.1.2024, respectively, and the Petitioner's rejoinder to the replies of MPPMCL and MSEDCL vide affidavits dated 29.1.2024, which have been dealt with in the succeeding paragraphs. The final hearing in this matter was held on 27.2.2024, and the order was reserved. However, the order could not be issued before Shri Arun Goyal, Member, demitted the office. Accordingly, the matter was re-listed for the hearing on 8.8.2024. During the course of the hearing, the representative of the Petitioner submitted that the pleadings had been completed in the matter and that arguments had been heard, and requested the Commission to issue an order on the basis of the information already on record. Considering the submissions of the Petitioner’s representative, the Commission directed the parties to file their respective written submissions/notes of argument, if any, within a week’s time, with a copy to the other side. However, no written submissions have been received from the parties. 7. Having heard the representatives for the Petitioner, learned counsel for MSEDCL and having perused the documents on record, we proceed to dispose of the Petition. 41. The Petitioner has submitted Form-5 wherein particulars about tree/crop compensation 43. We have considered the submission of the Petitioner. It is not clear from the submission of the Petitioner whether the Petitioner has paid compensation based on the orders of the Government of Gujarat or the orders of the District Magistrate. Therefore, the Petitioner is directed to clarify/ furnish the following at the time of truing up for review: 48. The Petitioner has submitted that during construction, severe RoW issues were encountered due to the farmer’s agitation demanding higher land de-valuation compensation. Accordingly, the Petitioner requested the district administration to conduct an assessment of the compensation towards RoW as well as provide necessary support and police protection to resolve the RoW issues. The Petitioner has further submitted that the progress of 51. A chronology of events resulting in the delayed commissioning of Asset-1 submitted by the Petitioner is as under: 60. The Petitioner has further submitted that during the construction, severe RoW issues were encountered due to the farmer’s agitation demanding higher land de-valuation compensation. Severe RoW obstructions were prevailing due to the demand for higher compensation in stringing work since farmers were not accepting the land compensation in the corridor at 7.5% of the land value and demanded the compensation as per the Central Government Guidelines. The Government of Gujarat Resolution dated 31.12.2021, increasing the land compensation in corridor from 7.5% to 15% of the land value was passed after detailed deliberations and consideration of the farmers requests on improving the compensation as indicated in the guidelines dated 14.8.2017 of the Gujarat Government. Even after the Government of Gujarat Resolution dated 31.12.2021, farmers at some locations were not cooperating and obstructed the construction activities and, therefore, the work was carried out under police protection. MSEDCL has contended that as regards the delay due to the RoW issues, the Petitioner cannot be granted the relief in view of the principle settled by the Commission in its order dated 23.6.2023 in the Petition No. 470/MP/2019 holding that the delay due to RoW issues is not something which cannot be anticipated by a transmission licensee and hence cannot be considered for any relief. 61. It is noticed that the Petitioner faced severe RoW issues in the commissioning of Asset1 due to the farmer’s agitation demanding higher land compensation. After the approval of the IA dated 21.5.2020, the Petitioner, vide letter dated 9.6.2020, informed the District Administration of Navsari and Surat districts of the assessment of compensation towards the land. Additionally, the Petitioner also made correspondence regarding the RoW issues and requested fixing the land rate vide letters dated 16.9.2020, 7.1.2021, 7.2.2021,12.3.2021 and 7.6.2021 to the respective authorities. Moreover, the Petitioner also took up the matter for subject to the submission of information by the Petitioner as sought in the Paragraph above. 94. The Petitioner has sought reimbursement of the fee paid by it for filing the Petition and publication expenses. The Petitioner shall be entitled to reimbursement of the filing fees and publication expenses in connection with the instant Petition directly from the beneficiaries on a pro-rata basis in terms of Regulation 70(1) of the 2019 Tariff Regulations. 106. This order disposes of Petition No. 55/TT/2023 in terms of the above findings and discussions. Order in Petition No. 55/TT/2023 _Page_ **_60_** _of_ **_61_** CERC Website S. No. 621/2025
